old_caption: The video captures a young woman dancing energetically in a brightly lit dance studio. She is dressed in a vibrant yellow and white striped t-shirt paired with a white tutu skirt, complemented by bright yellow socks and white sneakers. Her long dark hair flows freely as she moves rhythmically to the music. The studio features a large mirror on one wall, reflecting her dynamic movements and adding depth to the scene. The floor is a light wood, and the ceiling is equipped with recessed lighting, enhancing the overall brightness of the space. As the video progresses, the woman performs various dance steps, including arm movements and leg kicks, showcasing her enthusiasm and skill. The camera remains stationary throughout, focusing on capturing the fluidity and energy of her dance routine.

caption: The video captures a woman dancing in a bright studio with white walls, a light wood floor, ceiling spotlights, and a large mirror wall. Seen mostly from behind, she wears a yellow-and-white striped top, a white flared mini-skirt, yellow leg warmers, and white sneakers. The mirror shows her front reflection smiling, so the same figure appears twice in the fixed frame. Her arms move from bent positions near her chest into crossing motions in front of her torso and face. They lift upward with elbows bent and fists raised beside her head. She holds that raised-arm pose as her body sways and pumps through small weight shifts. Her stance narrows from a wide leg position to feet drawn close together, then the feet part again into a wider stance, with subtle torso rotations and hair swings visible in both her and the reflection.

An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.

processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.
